title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: The Signed Initial Declaration Behind a Review Decision
content:
## Clause

A decision on a Dangerous Goods Acceptance review answers the shipper's own signed statement of what it is shipping. It therefore presupposes that the declaration file of the acceptance holds the initial declaration in signed form, which the file shows as a submission of the initial type whose outcome is signed. A file without such a submission offers nothing to decide upon: its status remains under review and no decision is entered.

## What the declaration file may show

| Initial declaration on the file | Signed initial declaration present | Can a decision be entered on this ground |
|---|---|---|
| signed | yes | yes |
| awaiting the shipper's signature | no | no, the file stays under review |
| returned for correction | no | no, the file stays under review |
| withdrawn | no | no, the file stays under review |

## Points of judgement

**Does a signed amendment stand in for the initial declaration?** No. The ground concerns a submission of the initial type; an amendment is a different type of submission.

**Who can supply the signature?** Only the shipper can sign its declaration.
